name: feature_amihud_illiquidity
source: Amihud, Y. (2002). Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects. Journal of Financial Markets 5(1), 31-56.
license: citation and own summary only; no full text stored
claim: The average ratio of a stock's absolute daily return to its daily dollar trading volume (a price-impact illiquidity proxy) is positively related to its expected returns, both cross-sectionally and over time.
conditions: not crypto-specific; must be re-tested on crypto before use

name: feature_vpin_flow_toxicity
source: Easley, D., López de Prado, M. M., O'Hara, M. (2012). Flow toxicity and liquidity in a high-frequency world. Review of Financial Studies 25(5), 1457-1493.
license: citation and own summary only; no full text stored
claim: Volume-synchronized probability of informed trading (VPIN) tends to rise ahead of liquidity-induced stress events, including the 6 May 2010 flash crash discussed by the authors.
conditions: not crypto-specific; must be re-tested on crypto before use

name: feature_vpin_flash_crash_contradiction
source: Andersen, T. G., Bondarenko, O. (2014). VPIN and the flash crash. Journal of Financial Markets 17, 1-46.
license: citation and own summary only; no full text stored
claim: Counter-evidence: under an independent replication, VPIN did not reach an unusually high level before the 6 May 2010 flash crash, and its apparent predictive power appears largely mechanical, driven by choices in volume bucketing and trade classification.
conditions: same period as the original VPIN flash-crash study
not crypto-specific; must be re-tested on crypto before use

name: event_flash_crash_hft
source: Kirilenko, A., Kyle, A. S., Samadi, M., Tuzun, T. (2017). The Flash Crash: High-frequency trading in an electronic market. Journal of Finance 72(3), 967-998.
license: citation and own summary only; no full text stored
claim: During the 6 May 2010 flash crash, high-frequency traders did not change their trading pattern or trigger the crash, but their immediacy-demanding trades may have exacerbated the price move; the episode can be characterized as a large, fast price dislocation followed by a rapid reversal.
conditions: not crypto-specific; must be re-tested on crypto before use
